chunks: Here is a multitude rushing headlong with you. There is no welcome for them. They will roast in the fire.

key_terms.صَالُوا: They will roast or be baked (in the fire)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the crowd rushing with believers on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Sad, the disbelievers attempt to 'storm' into Paradise alongside the believers, but are rejected with the phrase 'no welcome for them,' highlighting the finality of their exclusion. Shia exegetes often view this as a confirmation of the distinct spiritual states of the righteous and the wicked, emphasizing that proximity in the hereafter does not guarantee shared destiny. This scene underscores the concept of 'Salu an-Nar' (they will be cast into the Fire), serving as a vivid warning against superficial faith.
